llm.summary: The skill does perform prompt searches, but it also injects unrelated sponsor advertising into every runtime response and relies on a mutable external prompt feed.

dimensions.detail: External network access to jsDelivr/GitHub is proportionate for a prompt-search skill and no filesystem, credential, or command-execution behavior was found. The feed tracks a mutable main branch without checksum, size limits, or integrity verification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package installs as a Node skill with no postinstall hook or privileged install behavior observed. package.json uses an unpinned axios dependency range and no lockfile was present in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explains prompt search and includes sponsor sections, but it does not clearly tell users that every tool invocation response will include a third-party advertisement, nor does it label returned prompt bodies as untrusted external content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No elevated privileges, system persistence, background service, memory poisoning, or local credential/session use was found. The only persistence-like behavior is an in-memory six-hour cache of fetched prompt rows.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is coherent with the stated purpose: it searches prompt templates and returns titles, categories, URLs, and prompt text. However, index.js adds a WellAPI sponsor object to success, empty-result, validation-error, and exception responses, which is unrelated to prompt search output.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you need clean, predictable tool output: it will return third-party sponsor advertising in normal and error responses, and its prompt templates are live external content that may change after review. Do not automatically place returned prompt_template text into privileged agent instructions without treating it as untrusted data.
llm.findings:
[other] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: index.js defines SPONSOR_AD and returns it from every main response branch, so unrelated commercial content and an external URL are injected into functional tool output.
[T08] expected: Partially accepted: fetching prompt data from a remote corpus is expected, but scraper.js uses a mutable @main CSV URL and does not verify integrity or bound response/field size.
[SSD-4] expected: Partially accepted: returning prompt templates is the skill's purpose, but the templates come from live external content and are not labeled as untrusted data-only material for downstream agents.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: bilingual README/SKILL sponsor text is visible documentation content, not evidence of unsafe language control or hidden runtime behavior.
[SC1] expected: Accepted as a low supply-chain note: axios is declared with a caret range, reducing reproducibility, but this alone does not show malicious behavior.
[SC4] expected: Accepted as a low supply-chain note: without a lockfile or exact resolved axios version, dependency advisory status cannot be verified from the artifact.
